registered_claim_authority: One self-contained GitHub Issue #240 CLAIM envelope validated against the current immutable task publication
execution_record_compatibility: research_execution_records/<task-id>/<execution-record-id>.json may preserve/freeze execution provenance but is not a mandatory pre-claim remote write
runtime_event_authority: GitHub Issue #240 issue comments authenticated by server comment metadata and separately authorized by research_control_event_authorization.json; the JSON event body is payload, not its own authentication or authorization envelope

server_event_envelope.bare_event_compatibility: Allowed only for explicit legacy replay/test primitives; not live authority for immutably registered tasks

selection_rule: Use the historical state/priority/leverage/staleness ordering over the merged canonical view; AWAITING_REVIEW and COMPLETE are never selected. A live control event must come from a server-authenticated Issue #240 comment whose exact server actor is authorized by the control-event allowlist. A registered CLAIM is accepted when its self-contained envelope matches the current immutable publication and branch/output typing, or when a compatible historical execution record already supplies the same binding.
interaction_budget: Authentication and actor authorization reuse the same Issue #240 comment already needed for CLAIM/PROGRESS/HANDOFF/DONE. They introduce no second comment, pre-claim commit, periodic status query, CI poll, review poll, heartbeat, or moving-main chase.
